items.title: Add red repro for silent validate idle-kill
items.context: Create a focused repro showing that a long silent validate command can trigger the lifecycle idle watchdog before the fix. Acceptance: the repro fails before implementation and does not pass by disabling the watchdog or skipping validate.
items.userSees: User sees the red baseline transcript: "validate stuck: 1 seconds without output; forcing exit" before the fix, and the smoke exits nonzero until heartbeat is implemented.

happy.desc: Red smoke command reproduces baseline idle-watchdog kill for a silent long validate command before the fix

edge.desc: The red repro fails because the idle watchdog kills active validation, not because validate is skipped or the per-command timeoutMs fires first

adversarial.desc: The repro would turn green only when heartbeat/progress keeps idle liveness alive, not by disabling the watchdog or using unlimited timeouts

items.title: Implement JSON-safe progress and heartbeat
items.context: Emit validate command start/end progress and flushed long-command heartbeat without corrupting --json stdout. Acceptance: long-running validate commands refresh parent lastActivity, stdout remains parseable JSON, and heartbeat does not extend command timeoutMs.
items.userSees: User sees stderr lines like "validate progress: command 1/1 started silent-long-command" and "validate heartbeat: command 1/1 silent-long-command elapsed", while stdout is a single JSON object.

happy.desc: validate emits command start, heartbeat, and command end progress for configured commands while stdout from --json remains directly JSON.parse-able

edge.desc: Heartbeat refreshes parent idle liveness but does not reset or extend the command timeoutMs wall-clock ceiling

adversarial.desc: Progress/heartbeat is flushed to stderr or another parent-visible side channel and never appears as trailing text in JSON stdout

items.title: Harden forced-exit cleanup and stale-lock classification
items.context: Ensure watchdog termination is two-stage where possible and validation locks are not considered active solely because of PID reuse. Acceptance: vanished or mismatched owners are stale, active owners are not stolen, and the approach stays host-neutral.
items.userSees: User sees stale-lock diagnostics that distinguish "active validation" from reclaimed stale locks; a vanished owner no longer blocks the next validate run.

happy.desc: Validation execution lock treats vanished or mismatched owners as stale and allows retry after forced exit cleanup

edge.desc: An active live validation owner with matching host-neutral liveness metadata is not stolen or reclaimed

adversarial.desc: PID reuse or stale holder metadata alone cannot make an old validation lock look active forever

items.title: Classify runner infrastructure failure separately from test failure
items.context: Forced exits and lifecycle runner failures should be reflected as infra failures, not ordinary test failures. Acceptance: watchdog/runner failures record infra_failure while ordinary test assertion failures still record test failure.
items.userSees: User sees timeout diagnostics that name the exact validate command and evidence classification "infra_failure" for runner/watchdog failures, while real test failures remain "FAIL" validation results.

happy.desc: Forced exits and lifecycle runner failures persist test evidence or validation result metadata as infra_failure, distinct from ordinary test assertion failure

edge.desc: Ordinary validate command assertion failures remain normal test/validation failures and are not mislabeled as infra_failure

adversarial.desc: A watchdog/runner timeout transcript cannot be mistaken for a passing test result or an assertion failure caused by user code

items.title: Verify story_advance TEST integration and safety regressions
items.context: Prove story_advance --phase=TEST survives active heartbeat and true hangs still fail closed. Acceptance: REVIEW -> TEST no longer dies from validate silence, diagnostics identify timed-out commands, and non-heartbeating hangs still fail.
